sections.html:
LONGWELL · LWDD7-5-EC

A compact blower with EC speed control

The DD7-5 combines a centrifugal fan with a 200 W electronically commutated motor. Its direct-drive arrangement, rectangular outlet flange and mounting base provide a defined starting point for integrating the fan into a ventilation assembly.

The published duty points cover 852–1,400 m³/h. Select a point that meets both your airflow and pressure requirement, then check the drawing against the space and connection available.

  • Power supply: 220 V, 50 Hz

  • Control input: 0–10 V or PWM signal

  • Exact model: LWDD7-5-EC

Manufacturer product photograph: LONGWELL.

sections.title: Detailed product overview
sections.html:
LONGWELL DD7-5 EC centrifugal fan — product overview

The LONGWELL LWDD7-5-EC brings the fan housing, impeller and electronically commutated motor together in a direct-drive assembly. The rectangular discharge flange provides a clearly defined connection point, while the base and supporting frame can be compared with the mounting arrangement in your equipment. This overview brings together the model information, product views and selection considerations so that the complete assembly can be reviewed before an enquiry or order.

For a replacement project, start with the full model reference rather than the DD7 series name alone. Compare the existing fan’s identification plate, connection dimensions and required performance with the information on this page. Two fans with similar names or a similar external appearance may have different motors, outlet dimensions or operating characteristics. The photographs illustrate the listed LWDD7-5-EC model; the dimension drawing and performance table provide the numerical reference for comparison.

sections.title: Airflow requirement
sections.html:
Understanding the airflow requirement

The published performance information describes a range of operating points rather than a single airflow figure for every installation. The highest listed airflow is 1,400 m³/h at zero static pressure. At a listed static pressure of 160 Pa, the corresponding airflow is 1,134 m³/h. These values should be considered together: the airflow required by the application and the pressure at that airflow form the duty point used to assess the fan.

When preparing an enquiry, include the target airflow, the calculated system pressure and a description of the equipment or duct connection. This gives a more useful starting point than selecting by maximum airflow alone. The performance table further down this description keeps the published airflow, pressure, speed and noise readings together, making it easier to compare a proposed duty with the available data.

sections.title: Motor, supply and control
sections.description: Motor rating, power supply and control signals.
sections.html:
Motor, supply and control

This model is listed with a 200 W EC motor, a 220 V / 50 Hz supply and 0–10 V or PWM speed control. The supply rating and control signal describe different parts of the connection. A controller therefore needs to be checked against the exact motor and its connection information. The product photographs show the motor position and external cable, while the model-specific wiring information is needed to identify individual terminals and connections.

For a replacement fan, record the control arrangement already used by the equipment as well as the mains supply. Include any controller reference with your enquiry so that the intended combination can be reviewed. The published specification does not identify a controller as part of the supplied package; confirm the items required for the complete installation when ordering.

sections.title: Dimensions and access
sections.description: Connection dimensions and space around the assembly.
sections.html:
Dimensions and access around the assembly

The drawing lists an overall height of 302 mm and a side-view overall length of 285 mm. The rectangular outlet flange is 222 × 220 mm, with fixing centres of 203 × 200 mm and eight Ø7 mm holes. These dimensions describe the illustrated connection and fixing arrangement; the flange’s outside dimensions should not be treated as the clear air opening.

Compare the drawing with the available position in the equipment, including the space around the inlet, the route of the cable and access to the mounting points. An overall envelope alone does not describe every connection detail. Photographs of the existing installation and measurements of its outlet and fixing pattern can help explain the intended fit when discussing a replacement.

Motor & control

Match the control to your system

LONGWELL specifies an EC motor with a 0–10 V or PWM control signal. These are control inputs; they should not be confused with the fan’s mains supply.

The catalogue lists Class F insulation, NMB ball bearings and an IP55 protection rating. Rotation is clockwise when viewed from the rotor.

Before connecting a controller, obtain the wiring information for this exact model and confirm signal compatibility. The published product page does not identify the terminal connections or a supplied speed controller.

sections.title: Selection and installation
sections.html:
Selection & installation

Plan the connection and available space

  • Required duty: provide your target airflow and system pressure together.

  • Electrical supply: confirm compatibility with the stated 220 V / 50 Hz rating and the chosen control signal.

  • Mechanical fit: compare the drawing with your outlet, mounting position, inlet clearance and service access.

  • Application: confirm suitability for the air being moved and the operating temperature before specifying the fan.

  • Installation: use the model-specific instructions to determine wiring, support, guarding and any required accessories.

The published page does not provide rated current, net weight, temperature limits or terminal assignments. Contact us with the exact model code and your requirements so these details can be checked before purchase.

Rear view of the same manufacturer-listed model.

sections.title: Product questions
sections.description: Four existing DD7 questions and answers.
sections.html:
Product questions

Frequently asked questions

Will it deliver 1,400 m³/h through any duct system?

No. That figure is the published point at zero static pressure. Ductwork, fittings and other components contribute to system resistance. Select the fan using the required airflow and pressure together.

Is DD7-5 the same as every fan sold as DD7 or DD7/7?

No. Use the complete model code LWDD7-5-EC when comparing specifications or asking for a replacement. Similar series names do not establish interchangeability.

Is a speed controller included?

The manufacturer specifies 0–10 V / PWM control capability but does not list the package contents. Confirm the controller, connectors and any other accessories required with your order.

What should I confirm before purchasing?

Confirm the duty point, electrical compatibility and mechanical fit, along with current availability, delivery arrangements, supplied accessories and applicable warranty terms. The technical data below does not establish those commercial details.

Commercial kitchen extraction

A system that fits your kitchen

Every kitchen has its own equipment layout, available space and route for extraction. We design and install ventilation systems that bring the canopy, ductwork and fan together around these requirements.

The installation shown here places the canopy directly above the cooking line, alongside the surrounding metal wall panels. Reviewing the equipment positions and site measurements helps establish how each part of the extraction system will fit.

sections.title: Considered from the kitchen to the exterior
sections.description: Installation details with a second photograph.
sections.html:
Ductwork and installation

Considered from the kitchen to the exterior

The ductwork route is an essential part of planning a kitchen ventilation installation. Available space, changes of direction and the points where ductwork passes through the building all need to be considered together.

This exterior view shows a rectangular duct section with a formed transition at its base. Our service covers ductwork design and fabrication, fan installation and commissioning. For a quotation, send a kitchen plan and photographs of the proposed route.

blog.title: Fabrication brief article sections
blog.sourceLabel: Preparing a Clear Brief for Stainless Steel Fabrication

sections.title: Article introduction
sections.html:
A fabrication brief brings the essential project information into one place. It describes what is required, how the equipment will be used and which details are confirmed. This helps a fabricator assess the scope without relying on assumptions scattered across photographs, sketches and messages.

The brief does not need to begin as a complete technical drawing. It does need to distinguish known information from dimensions or design decisions that remain provisional.

sections.title: Define the item and its purpose
sections.html:
Define the item and its purpose

Each item should have a clear description and reference. For a commercial kitchen project, that might be a stainless steel preparation table, sink unit, extraction canopy or wall cladding section.

The description should explain the intended use and its relationship to nearby equipment. A short account of the working arrangement is often more informative than a list of dimensions without context.

sections.title: Organise dimensions on a drawing
sections.html:
Organise dimensions on a drawing

A sketch should label the overall length, depth and height using consistent units. Sink positions, openings and connection points should be measured from identified reference edges.

Estimated dimensions should be marked as such. Where a measurement still needs checking, noting that uncertainty is more useful than presenting it as a production dimension.

sections.title: Give photographs a clear purpose
sections.html:
Give photographs a clear purpose

A wide view establishes the location and surrounding equipment. Detail photographs record the connections, obstructions or existing surfaces that affect the fit.

Numbering photographs and referring to them on the sketch helps connect the views. For an existing installation, it is also useful to identify which equipment will remain and which elements belong to the proposed work.

sections.title: Record materials, finishes and quantities
sections.html:
Record materials, finishes and quantities

Known material and finish requirements should be included with the drawings. Undecided details should be listed for confirmation so they are not replaced by unrecorded assumptions.

An item schedule should distinguish identical items from different versions. Separate references are useful where units share an overall size but have different sink arrangements, openings or connection positions.

sections.title: Describe the site requirements
sections.html:
Describe the site requirements

Installation information should cover the location, access route and any restrictions on when the area is available. Doorways, stairs and fixed equipment may affect how a fabricated item reaches its position.

The brief should identify the installation work required and any connections being coordinated with other trades. A target programme can be recorded without treating an unconfirmed date as an agreed commitment.

sections.title: Maintain a clear revision record
sections.html:
Maintain a clear revision record

Drawings, photographs and written requirements should use consistent item references. When a detail changes, the current revision should replace the earlier instruction in the project record.

A clear brief allows the specification and quotation to develop from the same information. It also creates a useful reference for checking the equipment and installation against the agreed scope.
